headline_marked: [[112 bodies, 40 children]] recovered from Gaza rubble after 2 years
headline: 112 bodies, 40 children recovered from Gaza rubble after 2 years
summary: Palestinian families held a mass funeral for 112 victims, including 40 children, whose bodies were recovered from the rubble of an Israeli airstrike that destroyed a residential building in Gaza City over two years ago.
details: Palestinian families conducted a mass funeral for 112 victims, including 40 children, whose bodies were recovered after being buried under the rubble of a residential building destroyed by an Israeli airstrike in Gaza City more than two years ago. The bodies were unearthed on Tuesday, August 4.

The mass funeral and burial on Tuesday was one of the largest since the ongoing war in Gaza began. It is estimated that the bodies of at least 157 other people still remain buried under the debris in the same location.

Israel launched its military operation in Gaza following Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. While nearly three years have passed, the recovery of bodies from rubble remains a rare occurrence.

Ahmad Alhendawi, Director for the Middle East, North Africa, and Eastern Europe at Save the Children, described the heartbreaking scene in Gaza. He stated that many families were finally able to bury their loved ones, emphasizing the profound suffering of not being able to do so after a child's death.

Alhendawi attributed the delay in recovering bodies to restrictions imposed by Israel, which he claims are hindering the access of rescue and search teams. He noted that essential heavy machinery, specialized equipment, and forensic assistance needed for the recovery are also being denied entry.
He urged for the immediate lifting of these restrictions to ensure families' rights to recover, identify, and mourn their loved ones. Alhendawi also called for an end to airstrikes in Gaza.

Children are paying the highest price in the war. International organizations' data highlights the devastating impact of Israeli military operations on children in Gaza. According to Gaza's Health Ministry, at least 21,000 children have been killed since October 2023, with over 44,000 injured, many sustaining life-altering injuries.

A UN independent international commission of inquiry stated in a report on June 23 that these harms to children were intentional. The commission's chairperson, Shrinivasan Muralidharan, indicated that evidence suggests Israeli security forces deliberately targeted and killed Palestinian children.

The UN report further detailed that children continue to be killed and seriously injured even after the ceasefire in October 2025, with Israel consistently disregarding the protection Palestinian children are entitled to under ceasefire agreements and international law.

The devastating impact of the war in Gaza extends beyond casualty numbers, with each death representing a family's collapse. Masha Yusuf, a mother of four and artist from central Gaza, shared her harrowing experience of losing her children, stating that Gazans are 'just numbers' to the Israeli military.

Yusuf described how her children's social lives have been almost completely destroyed by the war, with friends and teachers lost to the conflict. She noted the constant loss of loved ones, making it difficult to console children who have witnessed such widespread death.

Beyond grief and trauma, many children in Gaza are now taking on adult responsibilities to ensure their families' survival, including collecting water and queuing for food. Dr. Zida Alhakim, a specialist counseling psychologist, explained that this phenomenon, known as 'parentification' in psychology, occurs when children are forced into adult roles prematurely.

topic: trump warns iran to open hormuz strait
headline_marked: Trump warns Iran: [[Open Strait of Hormuz]] or face 'hit very hard'
headline: Trump warns Iran: Open Strait of Hormuz or face 'hit very hard'
summary: US President Donald Trump issued a stern warning to Iran, stating the strategic Strait of Hormuz must be reopened soon or the country will face severe consequences.
details: US President Donald Trump has threatened Iran with significant military action if the crucial Strait of Hormuz is not reopened promptly. The warning comes amidst ongoing discussions that could potentially resolve the standoff.

Trump stated in an interview with Fox News that "The strait is going to be open very soon, or they're going to get hit very hard -- and then the strait's going to be open." He indicated that negotiations are progressing positively.

Reports from Axios suggest that the US, Iran, and Oman are nearing an interim agreement to reopen the vital waterway. This deal, potentially announced as early as Wednesday, aims to ensure safe passage for global oil and gas supplies.
The proposed arrangement is reportedly a 60-day pact for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for international trade. This agreement could be extended if successful.

Under the potential deal, all maritime traffic heading into the Persian Gulf would utilize a northern shipping lane, while outbound traffic would be directed through a southern lane passing through Oman's territorial waters.
